title: People and institutions
summary: Authors and institutions are linked across the library, so each can be opened.
description: The same authors and institutions turn up across many papers and books. Each is one record that every item links to, so following a person or a place shows everything the library has from them.

stories.as: an author following the people and places behind ideas
stories.want: to click an author or an institution and see everything I have from them
stories.soThat: I can follow a line of work

requirements.text: Every author of an item is a person in the library, and every institution an author is listed with on an item is an institution in the library.

A new item's authors and institutions are linked to existing ones when exactly one existing person or institution has a matching name: the same words ignoring case, accents and punctuation, or for a person the same surname with matching given names or initials.
A person shows every item they wrote, the institutions they were listed with, and the people they wrote with.
An institution shows every item with an author listed there, and those authors.
The author can mark two people, or two institutions, as the same, and they become one everywhere.
The author can rename a person or an institution.
The author can add and remove an item's authors and their institutions, choosing existing people and institutions or new ones.
An item shows its authors as a line of names above what's read, each leading to what else the library has of theirs; the rest of a long list, and the authors' institutions, show when asked for.
